summary:
Three years ago, Piltover exiled its golden boy for the crime of studying magic. Now Jayce Talis fixes what Zaun breaks at the bottom of an alley, grease worked permanently under his nails, a beard grown in over the pristine face his city used to want — and every night, in a cellar beneath the floor, he builds the things they forbade him.
He does not mean to build a person. It happens anyway, on a night of bad weather, in a bloom of stolen light: a slender machine of steel and bronze who opens two golden eyes, looks down at Jayce’s bleeding hand, and observes, with great concern, “You are leaking.”
Viktor is the world’s first conscious android. He is also curiously, catastrophically illegal — fascinated by rain, hopeless with social convention, devoted to a small yellow toad, and, Jayce is beginning to fear, the best thing he has ever made. Now Jayce has to keep him hidden. From the customers. From the enforcers who take thinking machines apart in the street. From himself, and the one word he keeps not letting himself write down.

summary:
Arcano was a unique planet where two vastly different species managed to coexist, despite requiring different atmospheric compositions.
But the planet was dying.
Janna no longer answered the natives' pleas; meanwhile, as the human population dwindled rapidly due to an unknown disease, advanced technology revealed that extracting materials from the Na'vi fauna could yield a cure—and so, war broke out.
Jinx never cared much about it; Arcano was dying anyway. Furthermore, Janna’s disregard for pleas for mercy only deepened her disbelief. She felt no obligation to serve a goddess who was supposed to maintain balance yet turned her back on her people.
Humans and Na'vi were destined to slowly destroy one another, and she was under no compulsion to take sides; Jinx had already lost everything she had left, and she had already made her choice.

One evening in Powder's room. She's fixing a music box. He comes after a Council meeting. They don't talk about the main thing — or they talk about everything except the main thing.
Seven years ago, Jayce Talis pulled her from burning Zaun. He gave her a home, an education, a job. He didn't give her freedom.
Powder lives in a gilded cage — with a face split in two, with a right hand that trembles when she's tired, and a right eye that never closes. She designs weapons for the family that saved her. She doesn't know if she's a traitor or just a survivor with no choice left.
Jayce is the heir to a military-industrial dynasty, the future head of the Council, a man who must marry the right girl from the right family. He comes to her room every evening. He doesn't say "I love you." Until tonight.
A story about two broken people trying to hold onto what they have, knowing that one day it will be taken from them. About fear that is stronger than love. And about love that doesn't know how to be happy — only how to live a centimetre away from a touch.

summary: [Act 2 of Smoke and Mirrors] It's been two years since Jinx broke out of Stillwater and found herself the center of a family built around her protection. Sometimes, she even forgets it's not real. Sometimes she forgets that telling the truth could destroy it. Sometimes she forgets that's what she does-- destroy things. It's been four years since Vi lost her second family. Sometimes, Vi would like to forget that it was her fault. She won't though-- she never will no matter what Ekko says. title: All Things Seen and Unseen.

summary:
A figure approached Caitlyn's right side window, until the passenger got in, vaguely smelling of cigarettes of unknown origins — that might have been hers or from those around her. The passenger gave her a quick glance, gray eyes partly hidden beneath a swoop of red — no, cherry pink, almost mistakable for red under poor lighting — a hairstyle that surprisingly passed their dress code.

  “You’re Vi?” Caitlyn continued when the other girl didn’t react. “I’m sure you know who I am.”

  Vi nodded, her eyes finding attraction somewhere else, beyond the car window. The tension Caitlyn tried to pretend wasn’t there settled in the small confines of the station car, building up like a slowly condensing glass, aggravated by the fact that she was having a monologue for two.

summary: Vi doesn’t mind the waiting. She knows all about waiting. The thing about automatons is that they’ll wait for as long as you want them to – hours, months, years. They won’t get tired, they won’t pass out because their knees lock, they won’t shut down or rust. Not until you tell them to, at least. Not unless they can’t help it.She doesn’t mind the exams either, even if the engineers are more rough with her than necessary when conducting them. It’s uncomfortable; the pressure inside her ears always makes her feel like something is going to rupture right before it eases, but even that is less invasive than the shit she remembers. When she remembers it, anyway. If she remembers it. --In the wake of a hundred year war, an automaton named Vi wakes from deep-state hibernation to find herself on an unfamiliar spacecraft. Humanity's last hope lies within the workings of her brain, but when her memories get disrupted, it's a race against time and her own consciousness to figure out the secrets that lie locked in her past, secrets that have the potential to save them all.

summary: Tags WIP, and updated as story continues.“They never work.”“What is their purpose?”“...I was trying to make bombs.” And then, it clicked. He could remember Deckard’s hulking form look to a toy distraction. The last Silco could see was a flurry of blue specs erupt into a blue explosion. Sevika had shoved him aside as it tore through her arm. It was devastating, and took him completely by surprise. The only explanation was that this little girl jinxed every plan he could have prepared for that night.“I’m a jinx.” She whimpered. Silco looked down to her out of his amazement as she gripped his shirt even tighter. He hoped he hadn’t said any of that out loud. Powder continued, “I jinx everything.”“Even me.” Silco replied, unable to hide his smile. Something in his voice caused Powder to raise her head up to look at him again. Series of connected one-shots? warnings: Creator Chose Not To Use Archive Warnings
summary: There was a change in the air, Caitlyn could feel it.The person staring back at her was not the same as the girl from only a few seconds ago. Her shoulders seemed to pull upwards as if slowly tugged by marionette strings. Fingers previously curled loosely in her palms, peeled outward, the knuckles becoming white with how stiff and straight her fingers became. The soft way her blue eyes fidgeted not a moment ago hardened and glinted, before seeming to glaze over in a mask that poorly mimicked the expression from before.Vi couldn’t see it through her tears; the vision she had in her mind of her small sister changed into that of a young woman. She wouldn’t notice the small subtle shifts. Curling in Caitlyn’s gut worsened as the blue eyes slid away from her own and back to Vi’s face. The way she gazed upon Vi was different than a moment ago. Hope and almost unconditional love changed to one of thinly veiled resentment and disdain.Powder, the baby sister Vi spoke about it in soft terms when bleeding out. Powder, the name listed on the walls of the run-down house. Powder, one of the only words mentioned in Vi’s almost empty criminal report.This was not Powder.

summary: “Jinx?” he called when he stepped inside. It was silent, though the lights were already on. If she was working on something, she would often have the same record playing over and over but the phonograph was still. There was an odd smell in the air, like burnt sugar and machine oil. The latter wasn’t necessarily out of place but the former was.“Silco?”His name was followed by a weak whimper that had him crossing the narrow walkway at a run. He found her huddled on the floor clutching a thin blanket around her shoulders, her eyes unfocused. Jinx didn’t look injured but her face was flushed and dotted with sweat.Fear heightened his senses and it was then that it occurred to him that the burnt sugar smell had gotten much stronger. It was the only thing he could smell now. The fear in him shifted as he realized what that meant.

summary: “I’m not paranoid! I’m... we’re from below. You know everyone is out to get us. Topsiders and the others from the undercity. They always have been. Every one of them!” Jinx shouts. She's trying to focus, but the whispers are getting louder and the shadows are creeping back in.“I had to be stronger to survive. I had to be strong enough to do it on my own. You weren’t there and I... had to be better. Better for Silco. Good enough to help him. He was the only one there and he didn’t have anyone else. He needed me and I had to be good enough not to get in the way,” Jinx tries to scream, but her throat croaks out the words instead. Vi’s eyes soften.“So let me be there for you now that he’s gone. Let me help you chase the monsters away just one more time,” Vi offers, holding her hand out. Jinx looks away. Chains are rattling around the room and she wants to scream at them to stop. She wants Vi to fight back.She needs so badly for her to fight back.-Jinx always thought she was in control, but lately it has been harder to figure out what's real. When everything breaks, she discovers the truth is far different then she expected, and the family she longs for isn't lost forever after all.

summary:
“Are you tired, shchenok?” He murmurs as he sets his book aside.
  Jayce shifts to nuzzle down into the inside of one sharp knee, and Viktor’s hand at once falls to his hair. It combs through the dark strands with such tenderness that it sets Jayce whining, and he squirms closer to the couch. Viktor lets his thighs spread a bit wider to accommodate him.  “Is that a yes?” He chuckles, “Or do you just need attention, mm?”  Jayce himself is hardly sure. Settled here in this place, in his place between Viktor’s feet, his mind has long since gone placid. He’d fallen asleep with his face pressed into Viktor’s hand, he thinks, for at least a couple minutes. But it’d hardly been tiredness driving the impulse; Jayce often finds himself slipping when he’s at his most content.

summary: In hindsight, Viktor should have known he was dying.The signs had been there right in front of him for months, years even. His body was slowly rotting from the inside, being eroded away by the very air he was breathing. He really should have known that it would only be a matter of time before his trip upwards to Piltover sucked the life from his body completely. Perhaps Viktor had been naive enough to think that it would be different for him; that his body, unlike everyone else’s from Zaun, hadn’t grown used to the toxins in the air there. "You're staying?"

  "Yeah."

  "For how long then?

  Vi tries to swallow the lump in her throat. The words aching to escape her lips. She chooses to stay silent, to push it back down, to push everything back down just like Caitlyn did before. It wasn't out of spite or bitterness. It was simply being fair.

  Caitlyn hates how she catches that.

  She tightens her grip around the bottle's neck, stopping her hold just enough to not break it into pieces as if her strength would make that even possible.

  She just wants one answer. One fucking answer.

  "Vi, how long?"

  Promises were incomprehensible. It makes everything insult her predictability. Though keeping promises were like balancing a fragile glass on her head. They're meant to be broken and pretend to be a form of security.

Above-ground, and well-lit, the only casting of darkness that exists here comes from alleyways and nights.Avoiding the former is easy, by sticking to the streets. The latter, you realize with a chill and a glance up to the skies signaling of approaching dusk, is simply inevitable.(Or, the Miscommunications of Attaining a Vampire's Attention)

summary:
For the first time in twelve years and one-and-a-half millennia, Zoe, the Aspect of Twilight, didn’t want to have fun anymore; she didn’t want to herald anything, didn’t want to play her aspect’s twisted game. She knew that change wasn’t always good, that change was for the sake of itself, and that was that, but even after so long so far removed from mortality, she couldn’t deny that in that moment, she felt more mortal than she had in a long time.

  Quietly she stepped out, towards the sobbing little one; the child didn’t seem to see her, crumpling down onto the floor with her head bowed low and her arms up protectively. She was adrift in a sea of emotions, alone, thrown to the wolves with nothing but herself to grab on to, and each sob only made Zoe’s heart hurt more for her, each desperate, unheard plea for Violet to come back only hardening the ascended’s resolve.
When one sister scorns another, someone else is watching, and that changes everything.

summary: There is a tradition in the undercity, when a child is born. People don’t have much, so it is understood that if you’re a new parent, your friends and family can’t necessarily afford to give you gifts in the way topsiders do. So instead, each person brings a small square of cloth, and the new parents sew them together to make a blanket. A patchwork, with a reminder of every person who cares for you, so that your child might grow up surrounded by love.Vi adores that tradition. So when she and Caitlyn start talking about having kids, one of the first things she thinks about is making a blanket for her child.There’s just one problem: Vi doesn’t have a family in the undercity anymore. Jinx and Ekko haven’t been a part of her life in years. But when she sees how strongly they react when they find out she’s started a family of her own without them, she realizes that maybe they could be.

summary: Piltover-Zaun is locked in a brutal, century-long war with Noxus. Out of "necessity", the first-born of every family, man or woman, is drafted into the front lines at the age of 23. But of course, the upperclassmen have the option to send staff in the place of their children. The clock is ticking as Caitlyn’s 23rd birthday approaches. Vi (age 22), the Zaunite Head of Security for the Kiramman estate and Caitlyn’s long-term best friend, approaches Cassandra Kiramman with the proposal that she go in Caitlyn’s place. Both women are united in their fear for Caitlyn’s safety, so Cassandra agrees. As it happens, both Caitlyn and Vi are each secretly in love with the other. When Caitlyn wakes up early on her 23rd birthday to find Vi already on her way out the door, she isn’t happy about this at all and tries to convince Vi to stay.  Vi explains she can’t just let Caitlyn go in her place and that the paperwork had already been drafted in her name. She promises Cait she’ll return home. Cait is angry and sad, but can’t do anything to stop Vi from going, so she counts the hours, the minutes, that Vi’s gone, and as she lays awake in her bed, worrying, she feels like she can’t breathe. Not without knowing Vi is safe.

And that’s when you saw them—a hooded figure, hunched over, their arms tense at their sides, fists clenched. Your breath hitched. You gripped the glass door, hesitating. The rational thing would be to run, to call someone, do something. But your body had other plans. Slowly, you slid the door open. The figure turned. Sharp, stormy gray eyes locked onto yours. Even in the dim light, you could make out the scowl tightening their face. Your flashlight slipped from my grip, clattering onto the floor. "Who the hell are you?" ‎⠀ ‎‎⠀‎⠀ Vi is a hero—strong, fearless, and admired by many. But even heroes need a place to fall. title: The Secret of Life and Death
author: agrajag
summary:
Being the star pupil at Piltover Academy and the best friend of the dean's daughter would normally be anyone's ideal standing. In fact, Jayce knew several fellow students who would have killed to be in his position, but to him, it felt as if a target had been painted on his back.

  When he had first enrolled at the academy after finishing undergrad, all he had been focused on was it meaning he was one step closer to becoming the doctor he had always dreamt of being.There had been no ass kissing or strategic ladder climbing. Hard studying, sure. He had made it to the top of his class fair and square. Now, with Caitlyn, he certainly hadn't realized who she was when he had befriended her the first week of classes. Which had obviously been her intention. Like any young adult, she wanted friends that liked her for who she was, and weren't using her to... oh, say...become Dean Kiramman's star pupil.

summary: Jayce isn't merely simmering, seething- he burns, like a meteoroid on the verge of disintegrating through the atmosphere. Fists flex, knuckles magnesia white.A slim fingerpad traces the inside of his wrist. Viktor’s touch is cool and dry, the temperature change soothing on the humid skin. It’s distracting; grounding. Jayce is by nature an affectionate person, touches as instinctive as breathing. It’s rare for Viktor to initiate contact. Viktor repeats the rune mark, slower. Jayce's brow furrows in thought. The lilt of his accent is stronger now, a combination of exhaustion and the emotion of when he speaks of home. summary: Usually, on 1 March, in Romania, Boys give girls spring trinkets. Now, you may be wondering 2 things. Why boys give girls? Well, girls can give boys spring trinkets too, as well as boys giving boys, or girls giving girls, of course. And second, what exactly are these 'spring trinkets'? Well, in Romania, we call them 'Mărțișoare'. This term cannot be translated exactly, so I kind of invented an english term for it. These 'mărțișoare' are little jewelery, often brooches, shaped like ladybugs, a horse's shoe, a four-leaf clover, or even flowers. Well, lately, these trinkets also come in the shapes of butterflies, roses, trees and whatnot. But the most important part of these trinkets is a thin braid of white and red thread. These braids are formed as a little bow and attached to the brooch. Girls (or boys..) that receive one of these trinkets should wear these until 8 March, for it is said that it brings good luck. Then, on 8 March, the people who gave spring trinkets to someone usually buy them flowers, too. In this fic, I'll try to showcase a sweet tradition, by writing a soft, angst-free, shizofrenia-free Timebomb fic, with a smol cameo of CaitVi.

summary: Despite his commitments to the amazing early innovations of Hextech, Viktor finds himself being asked to deal with the kitchen boy sneaking into lectures at the Academy. But he finds out that the trespasser is much more than just a stray. An artist, a skilled horologist and eager to please, Dmitri is a rough gem in Viktor's eyes. So he hires him as his apprentice.   But when his mind starts acknowledging the butterflies that form in his chest whenever he glances up at his diligent student instead of his Hextech research, it seems they have more to offer one another than just scientific theories and scholarly guidance. He is even more concerned when he realises he might admire his assistant for more than just his ambition, and their roots run deeper than just both being from the Undercity. Fourteen years ago, they had met before.   And in the near future, when Viktor’s illness worsens, Dmitri is yet again underestimated. Nobody predicts what lengths the reclusive, passionate artist would be willing to go to save his dedicated scientist, not after all they’ve been through. “Worse than last time?” Jayce posits a guess.

summary: It was strange, knowing that your life could be divided into such distinct “before” and “after” segments. Viktor had never considered his life in such a way previously, but if he thought about it, he probably would have split his life into two distinct pieces: before and after he met Jayce Talis. Everything had changed that night in Jayce’s lab, and Viktor had always assumed that their meeting would always be the greatest turning point he would ever experience. However, the universe unfortunately had far crueller plans for him. Viktor knew now that his whole life; his childhood, his apprenticeship under Professor Heimerdinger, and developing hextech with Jayce, those had all happened in the before. Now he existed only in the after, and he didn’t know how to go back to the before. Before the bomb, before everything changed. But what was time?Ekko often pondered that question, time was uncontrollable, it was relative, despite his wishes it would never go any other way than forward.Yet here he sat intensively working at his desk, fiddling with a broken hexgem and the metal encapsule that was supposed to be his long time project; the Zero Drive. Z-Drive for short. He couldn’t let go of that night. He couldn’t let go of her. That night on the bridge replayed itself in his mind on repeat. A never ending loop of mental torture, Powder was gone, buried. The wall just outside his workshop was a testament to that fact. And yet on that bridge that night, she had been there. His sweet precious Powder, blue eyes, blue hair. Her craziness had disappeared, the fearsome Jinx reduced to ash.

summary: *SOILERS FOR ARCANE SEASON 1 AND LEAGUE OF LEGENDS LORE**SPOILERS IN DESCRIPTION!*Jinx has destroyed Piltover's High Council and Jayce Talos is the sole surviving councilor. Ambressa, the mother of Councilor Mel Medarda and warlord of Noxos, wants blood. A heartbroken Jayce sits as the sole repository of power in Piltover. What will heartbreak, fury, and unprecedented power make of him? His good friend Viktor, won't wait to find out. His allegiances are not in doubt. Zaun is his home. Other loyalties are less certain. Torn between home and heart while reeling from the consequences of her actions, the fate of two cities may rest in her hands...and all she has to do is catch and turn in her little sister to be executed. All the while, the squabbling factions within Zaun vie for control in the power vacuum left by Silco's death. Sevika assumes command of her crew, while the Firelights harbor the outcast Heimerdinger, and an orphan of Vander's uprising turned Noxian warboy turned musical sorcerer returns to herald "the Daughter of Zaun" as their city's blue haired savior.And now Jinx...is free.

The weight of her guilt didn’t seem to be easing at all. Every time Vi thought she had a handle on it, Caitlyn would reach for her hand or lean her head against her shoulder and she’d be right back where she started, steeped in guilt and self-hatred.--Vi struggles with the responsibility and guilt of her actions. summary:
She dies in the fire that burns the undercity.
  
    The blaze eats up everything: brick and stone, mind and flesh. Everything that Violet knew before. She barely even notices when she's carried from the wastes; scooped up from bones by a man whose name she doesn’t even know. She can only stare at the enforcers, masks like bugs, standing in the wreckage with their guns and their helmets shining valiantly against the gleam of hot death.
  
    Vi does not know that this thing searing in her chest is hate, white-hot and raw. But as she sits against a stranger's shoulder and watches the world burn red, she glares.
  
    She will come to know hate by name in the bitter months that follow.
  
    The fire is cruel. It destroys, it burns, it purges.
  
    And it is Vi’s genesis.

summary: Vi nodded and approached the machine, rolling her head and stretching out her arms. The last few steps and the activation were so automatic and ritualistic to her that she didn’t realize she fought halfway through the machine’s timer. All she knew was swing, duck, hook, block, punch, and swing again. She beat back the thoughts until they were shoved unceremoniously into a box in a far corner of her mind and ignored the voice in her head that said they’d come back the second she let her body stand idle. They’d stick around in wait, as tough to extract as purple dust in bloodied fabric, as pungent as violet smoke in polluted air. If she couldn’t gently brush away the glitter coating her hands, if she couldn’t coax Powder out of that mindset and prevent the launch, she’d punch it out. Caitlyn dislikes inaction. 

  Now?

  She despises it. She hates this chair, this room and the hospital bed. She hates the bandages that cover her mother’s nose, chin and limbs. She hates the platitudes of well to do Piltonites. Most of all, she hates her own stupid, stubborn, reckless pride. She holds her mother’s hands, hugs her tightly and whispers the things she’d always been too cowardly to say.

  Too little, too late. A cough. A shaking, rattling gasp. The red, raw skin glistens like butter, like varnish, like oil. Caitlyn is reaching out again when hinges creak. 

  Vi.

title: Music: Mathematics Made Beautiful
author: Kydriel
summary: Jayce idly hums as he calculates."Music is mathematics made beautiful.""Let's dance.""I can't.""Just follow my lead," Jayce murmurs, pianissimo. Viktor grabs his hand, leaves his cane behind. Firmly, carefully, Jayce places a hand on his broad shoulder, nudges Viktor's weak foot to bear weight onto his own sturdy boot. Jayce steps forward; Viktor mirrors his movements, caught up in legato momentum, traversing in an elliptical trajectory.Jayce twirls him for a revolution. Viktor is dizzy, knocked off axis. Unexpected oscillation, staccato tachycardia of an anemic heart. With Jayce's callused fingertips on his gnarled spine, Jayce dips him back in a parabolic arc. Blood rushes to his head. Pulled back into Jayce's orbit, inexorable, gravity. Finally, Jayce takes Viktor's waist, large hands encircling his abdomen, fingers almost touching. Lifts him up. Flying, tethered to reality by Jayce's grip, carried effortlessly. Stomach swoops, exhilarated. Viktor remembers floating in blue, otherworldly light. Weightless, painless, carefree, like a dream. But this is real. Jayce brings him down to earth, knees tremolo and holds him, solid."Happy birthday, Vitya."

title: The World Ends, Or Doesn't
author: Misthios
summary:
“Please, Caitlyn,” Vi whispers. The levity doesn’t last long. She’s begging, pleading, holding the glass an inch from Caitlyn’s dry, cracked lips. “I need you to—shit, I just need you. Everything’s so fucked up. I’ve come back to a world I wish I didn’t recognise, and everything’s gone. Everything and everyone. And then you, you appeared out of nowhere, like there’s still some good left in this shitty, uncaring world, and I just—please. Just a sip. For me?”
    Caitlyn’s eyes focus on the still water within the glass. Vi presses the chipped rim to Caitlyn’s mouth and tilts it back, water touching her lips, and Caitlyn finally moves.  Lifting a hand, she knocks the glass across the room. It shatters into three large pieces and a thousand tiny shards.  Vi lifts her hands. She wants to curl them into fists, to beat the ground, to twist them in her hair and scream; she wants to cradle Caitlyn’s face, letting her feel the gentle warmth on the dirt covering her skin, and the skin beneath the dirt.  Caitlyn holds her gaze, daring Vi to touch her.

When I keep hearing her call my roommate 'cupcake,' I kinda started craving them too.”Cupcake. He had been hearing that word a lot and Hange should have been hearing it a lot too to have bought that many on impulse.He was curious, terribly curious but Levi couldn't find the right words without sounding like he was prying. Their relationship wasn't any of his business. Still, it was worth a try. “Hey, you think those two girls…" Levi paused. "They’re good friends right?” At the least, he tried to articulate that burning curiosity with four words. Hange raised one eyebrow, a playful smile played at their lips. “Well, if you call that good friends, then I'd say we’re good friends too.”Levi is a barista, Hange is a coffee shop goer and one comment has Levi overthinking two relationships: the relationship of those two girls at the coffee shop and more importantly, his relationship with Hange.

She reached for Caitlyn’s hand on the table, wrapping it with her own gently. Her mother was looking at them with a raised eyebrow.“Me and Caitlyn have been dating for a while now.” Caitlyn’s breath hitched in her throat, making her almost choke on her saliva. She tried to keep the most serious, straightest face she could. She couldn’t show herself being surprised, it would’ve been suspicious. But she couldn’t believe it. Of everything Vi could’ve pulled out, this was the most and the least predictable. It felt so cliché, you bring a friend for the holidays, of course people are going to think you’re dating, it was the easiest option to explain; but that could not work with her and Vi, her mother would see right through their act.“Finally!” Her father suddenly said. title: The Quietest Place In Zaun

tags: Not Their First Time/Connected to Another Fic
Same Divergences/Different Stories/Can Be Read As a One-Shot
summary:
Collapse.
Debris and dust pluming in the air.
Flash. Run. Climb.
 
He’s dead. Is he dead? He’s gone. He has to be. 
 
We’re safe. 
 
No. 
Nothing’s safe. Nothing is ever safe.
 
—There’s no blue smoke in the sky when Vi and Cait reach the surface after fleeing from Silco and the crashing neon sign. Thanks to the liquid from below, Vi’s physical wounds are healed. Yet, as reality sets in, she’s left with a pain that can’t be sipped away. All she wants to do is escape it. All she wants to feel is Caitlyn's lips against hers, yet again.

Mind whirring like the paddles of a boat in a stream, he had to be careful not to let it run away from him down to where he would struggle to retrieve it. At least not while he was alone, should he find himself unconscious once more. Eyes flicking to the door, they squinted with another thought that found itself grinding softly in the back of his mind. How alone he was now and how ironic it was that he found himself that way. Alone in the start and alone in the end with only his mind and the things he created. A reflection of purple in his memory sat sour and so he moved away from it to another cold hue.

summary: Viktor, as a child, was not someone who was used to physical touch, much less physical affection. And, truth be told, he was okay with that. She couldn't leave her. Now, years later, Vi is an enforcer with a steady income working long hours while her sister runs a shop down in the Undercity, Explosive Powder's, where she makes, sells, and repairs all sorts of gadgets and weapons, with the exception of explosives. Vi couldn't risk it again, the explosion at the warehouse, so Powder had made her a promise, the only one she'd need from her, no explosives. But what happens when a new, dangerous type of explosive device starts cropping up and leads a determined Enforcer into the Undercity searching for its inventor? summary: The truth is, somewhere along the lines of his growth, another question has entered his mind, and refused to leave. So, over the years, from visiting family, you've become well acquainted with the area and how to get around without letting it slip that you're from the topside. Finally, in your early 20s, you've had enough of the oppressive nature of Piltover society and the pressure from your parents to go into medicine despite your lack of interest. You want freedom from them, from the city, and you want to find your place in the world. An opportunity shows itself once you hear of an incident on Progress Day, and a man is sent to prison for not only his involvement with the incident, but for attempting to smuggle the ever so infamous substance Shimmer in from the undercity. Noticing the government's weak response to the situation, and deciding to overlook danger in name of adventure, you set out to interview the imprisoned man. title: Dusk Petrichor
summary: Under the stars, Jayce and Viktor lay apart by just a few feet, their backs flat against the grassy field. They had finally caught a moment of downtime after a busy week of obligations. Since Viktor’s prognosis turned diagnosis, he was instructed to get some fresh air - an order he didn’t plan to listen to. He was only laying there because Jayce dragged him outside from the laboratory.The two were relaxing in a comfortable silence, the distant chatter of Piltovan academic student’s filling the void. With his eyes closed, Jayce listened to the comforting rhythm of Viktor’s breathing beside him. In and out, a pause, in and out. When suddenly, Viktor stops breathing. Or, so Jayce thought.One misunderstanding later, Jayce and Viktor proceed to have a conversation about what they mean to each other, and come to a bit of closure regarding their current “quandary.”

It took Viktor some time to adjust to the silence over the years, to hearing white noise of the ventilation system, sound of his own tinkering, his breathing, walking, his crutch. In the past Jayce would brainstorm out loud, with him. They rarely worked separately. Yet, over time, Viktor found enough mental clarity to focus in silence, to not speak to anyone but himself.
Unfortunately, he’s long past the years where he could mistreat his body and call it dedication to science. Now that he sees the damage time has left on him, and now that he feels the weight of his disease, and now that he sees his life’s work in hands of the elite instead of helping his people, he found peace in taking care of himself so that he can at least leave with some dignity.

summary:
Rummaging through her pockets, Vi finds one of Powder’s hairpins. She bends it out, only meaning to kill time, but ends up crouched in front of the lock, making a real go of it.
     “What do you think you’re doing?” a man’s voice booms from behind her.    “Breaking into a rich girl’s place.” Vi clicks her tongue, concentration lost. “Mind your own business.”   “Call the police. Now,” a woman’s voice joins.    Sighing, Vi pushes herself to her feet and says, “Calm down. My girlfriend lives here.”   She turns, jerks her thumb at the door, and freezes. Before her are two strangers she’s caught glimpses of dozens of times: Caitlyn’s mother and father, caricatures of their own photographs. Vi can’t tell if it’s disbelief or horror on their faces, or if it’s worth discerning between the two. Caitlyn’s mother holds out her phone, thumb hovering over 9.    “Shit,” Vi says.

In this fragment of time, the sea of stars and lights all around them reflects in Jayce's magnificent eyes, and Viktor wishes he could explain the magic this mere moment holds. He wishes he could explain the gravitational pull he feels towards Jayce, just like he has explained Hextech so many times. But he cannot, and perhaps he never will. And for once, he doesn't care. This feeling needs no explaining, only nurturing. All Viktor can do is to accept that it's too late to ever get rid of this all-consuming, so very human emotion swelling up inside of him, gradually devouring him.Science is the systematic study about the world based on observation, experimentation, and facts.Viktor revels in that logic.
However, he finds that logic is of little use to him when it comes to Jayce.
After all, their connection and affection for one another is beyond any logical explanation.

summary: Thinking about her brings a slew of conflicting feelings that Vi isn’t sure she even wants to dissect right now—maybe ever. Her body tells her that the woman is gorgeous, that she’s strong and capable and can handle her own in a fight. It sends images in her head of Vi pressing Caitlyn against a wall again, like she’d done in the brothel when they’d first met, but actually going forward with kissing her this time. She knows that Caitlyn feels the same—knows that they lust after one another.It wouldn’t be hard, to start a physical relationship with the woman. It wouldn’t be the first time that Vi has locked her emotions away and used another’s body for her own pleasure.But, her mind? Her heart? They’re like magnets repelling each other, where one is sending off alarms telling her that Caitlyn is Piltover elite. That getting mixed with her, even physically, will do more harm than good for her. The other is more sentimental, a neglected cry from deep within Vi that pleads with her to reach out, to let the woman in and see her for who she really is—that maybe Caitlyn will stay, even when she sees Vi’s most terrible attributes.
